text:
maya-devex: Quick heads-up — noticed compacted route header rollout (proxy -> compact X-RD-Route) is skewing quota attribution in the console :thinking_face:

sam-platform: Yep, saw canary yesterday. Per-route token counts down ~25-35% vs baseline. Looks like console mapping doesn't unpack the compact payload so it attributes to `unknown` bucket.

jin-py: @sam-platform can you paste an example header? I want to reproduce locally.

sam-platform: sure — example from proxy logs (trimmed):
```
X-RD-Route: cm91dGU6W3siZW50cnkiOiJwcm9tcHQiLCJwcm90b2MiOjJ9XS1jbXQ=
User-Agent: redwood-proxy/2.1.0
```

maya-devex: The compact encoding is base64 of a small json array. We agreed on that to reduce header size for mobile + browsers. But it means console ingestion needs a decode-pass before route normalization.

alex-ts: I pushed a tiny parser change to the console-mapper branch this morning but didn't realize SDKs were going to switch on the flag in prod.

nina-frontend: If console can't map it, dashboards show `unknown` route which breaks quota heatmaps and alerting. We need graceful fallback in the console and the SDKs.

jin-py: Proposal: SDKs send compact header by default when server announces `Accept-Compact-Route: v1` but fallback to legacy expanded `X-Redwood-Route-JSON` if we receive a 422/400 or if we see `X-RD-Route-Ack: unknown` in responses. That keeps rollout safe.

sam-platform: I like fallback. Also we should add a server-side opt-out header so customers can pin legacy behavior `X-RD-Route-Policy: legacy`.

alex-ts: For TS/JS SDK I'll add transparent fallback logic. Behavior: attempt compact, if server responds 4xx within first 5 requests -> switch to legacy for 10m then re-check. Should we also emit an event to telemetry so we can see rollouts failing?

maya-devex: Yes telemetry event required. Add `sdk.route.compact.fallback` with tags: sdk_lang, sdk_version, reason(code).

nina-frontend: Console UX asks for two things: 1) map compact->expanded for existing traces so historical charts aren't lost (we can decode at ingest), 2) dashboard flag showing percent of traffic using compact header.

jin-py: Quick sketch of SDK fallback (py):
```python
# pseudocode
if server_supports_compact and not forced_legacy:
    send_compact_header(route)
    if response.status_code in (400,422) and attempts < 5:
        emit_event('sdk.route.compact.fallback', reason=str(response.status_code))
        send_legacy_header(route)
```

sam-platform: One caveat: quota ledger deduping relies on canonical route id. If we accept both headers simultaneously during rollout we need a canonicalization step server-side to unify IDs, otherwise double-charging or missed attribution can happen.

maya-devex: Good catch. Action item: server team to ensure canonicalization table during rollout window. Fallback should not create new route ids — map to same canonical id.

alex-ts: I'll coordinate a small PR to the SDK repo with opt-in flag `compact_route: 'auto'|'force'|'legacy'` so customers can control. Default 'auto'.

nina-frontend: I'll add a console ingest job to decode compact payloads on historical rows and a dashboard tile for rollout progress (pct compact vs legacy). Small note — decoding old logs may be CPU-heavy; I'll add a throttle.

deploy-bot: canary-deploy redwood-proxy v2.1.3 started (canary region: us-west-2).

sam-platform: Running integration smoke now — will monitor `sdk.route.compact.fallback` events and console unknown count.

jin-py: I'll open a py-sdk PR with fallback + telemetry patch and a short test harness. ETA EOD PST.

alex-ts: Working on TS PR, will match behavior and add unit tests.

maya-devex: Great. Let's not flip the global flag until server canonicalization landed. Can we get that in 48h?

sam-platform: I'll own server task. Creating issue now and linking to this thread.

jin-py: PR: https://github.com/redwood/sdk-py/pull/198 (draft)

alex-ts: PR: https://github.com/redwood/sdk-js/pull/402 (WIP)

nina-frontend: Console ingest job created: https://go/console/issue/9876 — will start decode job on a 1% sample first.

maya-devex: Awesome — thanks all. Keep updates here. :thumbsup:
